headline: Senate resolution that would have blocked a proposed U.S. military sale to Israel did not advance.
what_it_does: This joint resolution would have stopped a proposed sale of certain U.S. military equipment and services to the government of Israel. Congress can use this kind of resolution to block arms sales that the executive branch has proposed. The official summary does not list which weapons or services were part of the sale. On April 3, 2025, the Senate voted not to take it up, so the sale was not blocked by this measure.

who_it_affects.how: Israel would not have received the specific defense equipment and services covered by the proposed sale.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. defense companies supplying the sale
who_it_affects.how: Companies that would make or provide the items in this sale would have lost that business.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. executive branch (State and Defense Departments)
who_it_affects.how: These agencies would have been barred from carrying out this particular foreign military sale.
